items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold prices were lower and spot silver prices were higher in late U.S. trading Tuesday, as weakening housing activity and lower Treasury yields failed to overcome persistent inflation concerns and expectations for additional Federal Reserve tightening. Crude oil prices reversed sharply from their morning highs amid conflicting reports about possible renewed U.S.-Iran negotiations, easing some inflation pressure and helping U.S. equities recover from early losses. At the time of the latest afternoon price reading, spot gold was trading near $4,122.50 an ounce, down $17.40, or 0.42%, while spot silver was trading near $57.800, up $0.825, or 1.45%. Tuesday's U.S. economic reports provided further evidence that elevated interest rates are weighing heavily on the housing market. September housing starts declined 5.2% to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.221 million units , below expectations for approximately 1.305 million and down from an upwardly revised 1.288 million in August. Single-family construction fell 4.6% to an annual rate of 859,000 units, while building permits declined 0.2% to 1.400 million units. Housing demand weakened more sharply, with September pending home sales plunging 7.3% from August and 11.3% from a year earlier, reaching their lowest level since the index began in 2001. The declines followed Monday's drop in the NAHB housing market index to 29 from 32, reflecting deteriorating buyer traffic, elevated mortgage costs and weakening builder confidence.
